moat_against: Vertiv, Eaton, ABB, Schneider Electric and Legrand are larger and sell into the same data-center budgets
Enclosures and fastening are partly commoditized — limited pricing power outside specified niches
Hyperscaler customers have strong bargaining power and can dual-source
Growth is concentrated in one AI data-center capex cycle that can pause or reverse
Acquisition-led growth (Avail) adds integration and amortization load
moat_for: Brands specified into electrical codes and engineer designs (HOFFMAN, ERICO, CADDY, SCHROFF) — spec-in creates switching friction
Global distribution and channel reach across infrastructure, industrial and commercial verticals
Liquid-cooling scale and hyperscaler relationships in data centers, with capacity being added ahead of demand
Broad, code-driven portfolio (enclosures, connection, fastening, protection) sold as systems, not parts
moat_justification: Spec-in brands (HOFFMAN, ERICO, CADDY, SCHROFF) embedded in electrical codes and engineer specifications, a global distribution network, and early liquid-cooling scale with hyperscalers give real switching friction and pricing power; but Vertiv, Eaton, ABB, Schneider and Legrand are larger rivals selling into the same data-center budgets, enclosures/fastening are partly commoditized, and the current growth surge rides a single AI capex cycle.
name: nVent Electric plc
one_liner: Good business, moat 6/10, riding the AI data-center boom — but at $152.72 even the super-bull case returns only 14.4%; weighted IRR 8.7%, IV@15% $66.33. It clears 15% only at or below $66.33.
